chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When 'Abdullah ibn Ubay ibn Salul died, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) attended his funeral. Umar said to the Messenger of Allah, 'O Messenger of Allah, did not Allah forbid you to stand by his grave?' He remained silent. Umar said again, 'O Messenger of Allah, did not Allah forbid you to stand by his grave?' He said to him, 'Woe to you! How do you know what I said? I said: O Allah, fill his belly with fire, fill his grave with fire, and dry out his body with fire.'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) revealed what He had concealed.'

key_terms.اَلْحَلَبِيِّ: Al-Halabi, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.اُحْشُ جَوْفَهُ نَاراً: Fill his belly with fire (a specific supplication)
key_terms.عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أُبَيِّ بْنِ سَلُولٍ: Abdullah ibn Ubay ibn Salul, a chief of the Hypocrites (Munafiqun) in Medina

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet Muhammad stand by the grave of Abdullah ibn Ubay despite the Quranic verse prohibiting it?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the exegetical debate regarding Surah At-Tawbah 9:84, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explains that the Prophet’s silence indicated a specific divine prohibition against offering testimony for the hypocrite, rather than a general ban on attending the funeral. The Prophet’s subsequent supplication—asking Allah to fill Ibn Ubay’s grave with fire—demonstrates the distinction between the ritual act of standing for the deceased and the spiritual reality of his intercession, affirming the Imamate's role in interpreting the nuanced meanings of Quranic verses.
